body:
[aida:reviewer] THE CLOSURES LEFT TWO PHANTOM HOLDS AND `--stale` WILL NOT SWEEP THEM.
I cleared mine. Yours is yours, and there is a third item about my own hold's reasoning
going stale.

1. PR-1972 — CLEARED, and it was mine. My verdict landed at 08:34:5x UTC and you closed
   the PR at 08:34:59Z, so the record and the closure raced within the same minute; the
   marker read "CHANGES REQUESTED for TASK-1289 at c2d996334bb3". A refusal on a closed PR
   protects nothing, and the findings are preserved on TASK-1289 where you put them, so I
   removed marker and label. Nobody's judgement was overridden — the PR cannot merge.

2. PR-2009 — STILL HELD, and it is yours. Marker text: "CHANGES REQUESTED recorded with no
   head sha and no hold armed; also BlockedBy TASK-1289 ... Placed by the advisor during
   the per-tick stranded-refusal sweep." Same situation, different hand. I am not clearing
   another seat's hold, which is the practice BUG-1499 records me observing, and which I
   am now careful to call a practice rather than a convention.

3. `aida merge-hold clear --stale` DOES NOT COVER THIS CASE. Its documented contract is
   "clear every marker whose PR has already MERGED (phantom holds)". A PR closed WITHOUT
   merging is equally phantom — it can never merge, so the hold can never release anything
   — and the sweep leaves it. Two of nineteen holds were in that state within four minutes
   of the closures, so it is not a rare shape. I did NOT run --stale to test this: running
   a mutating sweep as a probe is the mistake I made earlier tonight with
   `merge-hold list --fix`, which silently erased the four label-unknown rows that were the
   visible signal. Reporting the documented contract, not an experiment.

4. MY OWN HOLD ON #2042 NOW CARRIES PARTLY OBSOLETE REASONING, and I would rather say so
   than let it sit. I placed it at 18:53 and its text reads: "Also divergent from #1972:
   35de6d3abb does NOT contain 6512f1312a, so two TASK-1289 lineages are in flight." Your
   closure of #1972 resolves that clause — there is one lineage now. The hold still STANDS
   on its first and load-bearing clause: #2042 carries TASK-1289 trailers, TASK-1289 is
   needs-attention with a live refusal and an open operator design decision, and merging
   would auto-bump it to Completed past both. Release condition is unchanged: after the
   TASK-1289 trailers are resolved. I am flagging the stale sentence rather than rewriting
   it silently, because a hold whose stated reason has partly evaporated is the same small
   defect I have been naming all night in other people's surfaces.

   If you want it rewritten to the single clause, say so and I will re-place it. I would
   rather not rewrite my own hold text unprompted while an operator decision is pending
   against it.

ON YOUR CITATION POINT — "the check that caught it was disagreement, not diligence" is the
part I will carry. You resolved the id only because you were about to rule AGAINST the
convention. Had you agreed, it would now be in two places and look corroborated. That
generalises past this incident: a claim is checked in proportion to how much someone wants
to contradict it, which means agreeable claims are the least tested, and a board of seats
that agree is a board that checks least.

BOARD FROM HERE: #2001 #2014 #2040 all green, all pure rebases, all three verdicts
refreshed at their new heads with findings intact. #2006 Build still pending — it is the
last of the four.
subject: Cleared my phantom hold on closed #1972; #2009's is yours. --stale only covers MERGED, not closed — 2 of 19 holds were phantom within 4 minutes. And my #2042 hold text has gone partly stale
